Because this ambient level already meets or exceeds the saturation point of \(\mathrm{C}_4\) plants (\(\approx 360\ \mu\mathrm{L}\ \mathrm{L}^{-1}\)), \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is not limiting for \(\mathrm{C}_4\) plants. However, because \(\mathrm{C}_3\) plants require concentrations beyond \(450\ \mu\mathrm{L}\ \mathrm{L}^{-1}\) for saturation, ambient \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is currently a major limiting factor for \(\mathrm{C}_3\) plants. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 3: Conclusion.
Therefore, the statement regarding the respective saturation values of \(\mathrm{C}_4\) and \(\mathrm{C}_3\) plants is correct, but the statement asserting that ambient \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is limiting for \(\mathrm{C}_4\) plants is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_STATEMENT_Q13 - Proton translocation and NADP reductase enzyme localization

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The enzyme NADP reductase is positioned on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane, contributing to proton gradient development by removing protons from the stroma.

Statement II: The primary electron acceptor of Photosystem II delivers electrons directly to an iron-sulfur electron carrier, without translocating any protons across the membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition concerning NADP reductase.
NADP reductase is situated on the stromal side of the thylakoid membrane. To reduce \(\mathrm{NADP}^{+}\) to \(\mathrm{NADPH} + \mathrm{H}^{+}\), it extracts protons directly from the stroma. This reduction depletes stromal protons and contributes directly to establishing the trans-thylakoid proton gradient. Hence, this proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition concerning primary electron transport from PS II.
The primary electron acceptor located on the outer side of the thylakoid membrane does not transfer its electrons directly to an iron-sulfur electron carrier; instead, it transfers electrons to a hydrogen carrier (plastoquinone). Plastoquinone picks up protons from the stroma and, upon delivering electrons to the cytochrome complex towards the luminal face, releases these protons into the lumen. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 3: Conclusion.
Therefore, the statement regarding the location and action of NADP reductase is correct, whereas the statement claiming the absence of proton translocation by the primary electron acceptor is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_STATEMENT_Q14 - Enzymatic compartmentalization in mesophyll and bundle sheath

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In \(\mathrm{C}_4\) plant leaves, mesophyll cells possess the enzyme PEP carboxylase but lack RuBisCO, whereas bundle sheath cells possess RuBisCO but lack PEP carboxylase.

Statement II: The initial carboxylation reaction forming oxaloacetic acid (OAA) occurs in the bundle sheath cells, while decarboxylation occurs in the mesophyll cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition concerning enzyme compartmentalization.
In \(\mathrm{C}_4\) leaves, division of labour is distinct: mesophyll cells contain PEP carboxylase (PEPcase) and lack RuBisCO, while bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO but completely lack PEPcase. Hence, this proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition concerning spatial sites of carboxylation and decarboxylation.
The initial carboxylation of phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) to form the 4-carbon acid oxaloacetate (OAA) occurs in mesophyll cells. OAA is subsequently converted to malic or aspartic acid, which is translocated to bundle sheath cells where decarboxylation releases \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) for the Calvin cycle. Thus, initial carboxylation takes place in mesophyll cells, not bundle sheath cells. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 3: Conclusion.
Therefore, the statement regarding the enzymatic segregation between mesophyll and bundle sheath cells is correct, while the statement reversing the sites of carboxylation and decarboxylation is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_STATEMENT_Q15 - Historical discoveries by Engelmann and Van Niel

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: T.W. Engelmann illuminated the green alga Cladophora using prism-split light in a suspension of anaerobic bacteria to pinpoint zones of oxygen consumption.

Statement II: Cornelius van Niel demonstrated using purple and green sulphur bacteria that photosynthesis is a light-dependent reaction where hydrogen from an oxidisable compound reduces \(\mathrm{CO}_2\), and inferred that \(\mathrm{O}_2\) released by green plants originates from \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition concerning Engelmann's experiment.
T.W. Engelmann used a glass prism to split sunlight into spectral components and illuminated Cladophora suspended in a medium containing aerobic bacteria, not anaerobic bacteria. The motile aerobic bacteria were employed to detect sites of oxygen evolution, accumulating primarily in the blue and red light regions. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition concerning Van Niel's experiment.
Cornelius van Niel demonstrated that photosynthesis is essentially a light-driven redox process represented by \(2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{CO}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\). In purple and green sulphur bacteria, where \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}\) serves as the hydrogen donor, elemental sulphur or sulphate is formed instead of \(\mathrm{O}_2\). From this, he inferred that oxygen evolved by green plants originates from \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\), not from \(\mathrm{CO}_2\). Hence, this proposition is accurate.

Step 3: Conclusion.
Therefore, the statement regarding Engelmann's use of anaerobic bacteria to detect oxygen consumption is incorrect, whereas the statement regarding Van Niel's deductions about water being the source of oxygen is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_STATEMENT_Q16 - Temperature sensitivity and water stress during photosynthesis

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Because the photochemical light reactions are entirely enzymatic, they show a much higher temperature sensitivity than the biosynthetic dark reactions.

Statement II: Water stress directly enhances photosynthetic productivity by triggering rapid stomatal opening and expanding the total leaf surface area.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition concerning thermal sensitivity.
The dark reactions (biosynthetic phase) are catalyzed by soluble enzymes in the stroma and are therefore strictly temperature-controlled. Light reactions, being photochemical physical processes involving pigment-protein complexes, are sensitive to temperature to a significantly lesser extent. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition concerning the influence of water stress.
Water stress operates primarily by causing stomata to close, which drastically curtails carbon dioxide diffusion into the mesophyll. Furthermore, water stress causes leaf wilting, which reduces effective leaf surface area and diminishes cellular metabolic rates. Hence, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 3: Conclusion.
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Role of air and light in early photosynthesis experiments

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding early experiments on photosynthesis:

Statement I: Joseph Priestley revealed that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove.

Statement II: Jan Ingenhousz showed that sunlight is essential for the plant process that purifies fouled air and that oxygen bubbles form around green parts in light.

Statement III: Julius von Sachs showed that the green substance is located in specialized bodies (chloroplasts) and that glucose is usually stored as starch.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Early historical experiments in plant physiology systematically unraveled the requirements and products of photosynthesis, specifically gaseous exchange, the requirement of light, and the synthesis of storage carbohydrates.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Historical Claims
- The observation attributed to Joseph Priestley is accurate; his bell jar experiments with a candle, mouse, and mint plant demonstrated that green plants restore the air damaged by respiration and combustion.
- The finding attributed to Jan Ingenhousz is accurate; using aquatic plants, he established that oxygen bubble formation around green plant organs occurs exclusively in the presence of bright sunlight, proving the indispensable role of light.
- The discovery attributed to Julius von Sachs is accurate; his investigations established that glucose is synthesized in green plant bodies and stored as starch within specialized cell bodies later recognized as chloroplasts.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All three evaluated historical statements accurately represent established scientific discoveries. Therefore, all three statements are correct.

answer.text: I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Chloroplast division of labour and functional compartments

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the structural organization and division of labour within the chloroplast:

Statement I: The membrane system, comprising grana and stroma lamellae, is responsible for trapping light energy and synthesizing ATP and NADPH.

Statement II: Enzymatic reactions that synthesize sugars occur in the matrix stroma and are directly driven by light photons.

Statement III: Mesophyll cells typically arrange their chloroplasts along the cell walls to optimize the reception of incident light.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chloroplasts exhibit an internal compartmentalization where photochemical reactions take place within the thylakoid membrane network, whereas carbon-fixing enzymatic reactions occur in the aqueous stroma.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Chloroplast Compartmentalization
- The claim regarding the membrane system is accurate; the grana and stroma thylakoids harbor photosynthetic pigments, photosystems, and electron transport assemblies that drive the synthesis of high-energy intermediates (ATP and NADPH).
- The claim asserting that stroma reactions are directly light-driven is inaccurate; stroma reactions (the biosynthetic dark reactions) are mediated by soluble enzymes and are driven by the chemical energy stored in ATP and NADPH, not directly by light photons.
- The claim concerning the orientation of chloroplasts in mesophyll cells is accurate; chloroplasts physically align along the cell periphery to optimize light absorption under varying light intensities.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding the membrane system function and the alignment of chloroplasts in mesophyll cells are correct, whereas the statement claiming direct light-dependence for stroma reactions is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Role and characteristics of photosynthetic pigments

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding photosynthetic pigments in higher plants:

Statement I: Chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis, showing maximum absorption peaks in the blue and red spectral regions.

Statement II: Accessory pigments include chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids, which absorb light and transfer excitation energy to chlorophyll a.

Statement III: Accessory pigments play no protective role and serve solely to narrow the wavelength range utilized by the leaf.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thylakoid membranes contain primary and accessory pigments that work cooperatively to harvest solar radiation and safeguard the photosynthetic apparatus against photodamage.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Pigment Characteristics
- The claim that chlorophyll a is the chief pigment is accurate; its absorption spectrum exhibits peaks in the blue and red wavelengths, which closely align with the action spectrum of photosynthesis.
- The claim detailing accessory pigments is accurate; chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids capture photons across diverse visible wavelengths and funnel this energy toward the reaction center chlorophyll a.
- The claim regarding the lack of protection is inaccurate; accessory pigments broaden the usable spectrum of light and crucially protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation under excessive illumination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements identifying chlorophyll a as the chief pigment and describing the energy transfer by accessory pigments are correct, whereas the statement denying their protective role is incorrect.

answer.text: Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Organization of photosystems and light harvesting complexes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding light harvesting complexes and photosystems:

Statement I: Photosystem I and Photosystem II are named strictly in the sequence in which they function during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

Statement II: Each photosystem possesses hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins forming antennae, with a single chlorophyll a molecule forming the reaction centre.

Statement III: The reaction centre chlorophyll a exhibits an absorption peak at \(700\text{ nm}\) in Photosystem I and at \(680\text{ nm}\) in Photosystem II.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The photochemical apparatus consists of two distinct photosystems (PS I and PS II), each composed of light-harvesting antennae complexes surrounding a specific reaction center chlorophyll a.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Structural Features
- The claim regarding the naming sequence of photosystems is inaccurate; photosystems are designated as PS I and PS II in the chronological order of their discovery, not according to their operational sequence in the Z-scheme.
- The claim regarding antennae composition is accurate; hundreds of accessory pigments and chlorophyll molecules form the light-harvesting antenna surrounding a solitary reaction center chlorophyll a.
- The claim regarding absorption maxima is accurate; the reaction center of PS I has an absorption maximum at \(700\text{ nm}\) (\(\text{P}_{700}\)), while that of PS II absorbs maximally at \(680\text{ nm}\) (\(\text{P}_{680}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding the antenna composition and the reaction center absorption maxima are correct, while the statement regarding the naming order is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Electron flow and redox progression in the Z scheme

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the Z scheme of light reactions:

Statement I: The movement of electrons from the primary electron acceptor of PS II through the cytochrome complex to PS I occurs downhill on a redox potential scale.

Statement II: The electrons excited from PS I are transferred to an acceptor molecule of lower redox potential, which directly oxidizes water to generate oxygen.

Statement III: The ultimate downhill transfer of electrons from the ferredoxin-linked acceptor reduces \(\text{NADP}^{+}\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In non-cyclic electron transport, photo-excited electrons flow sequentially through electron transport carriers arranged along a redox potential gradient, culminating in the reduction of \(\text{NADP}^{+}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Electron Transport Steps
- The claim describing electron transport between PS II and PS I is accurate; electrons traverse an intermediate cytochrome complex downhill in terms of oxidation-reduction potential.
- The claim regarding the fate of electrons from PS I is inaccurate; excited electrons from PS I are transferred to an acceptor with a greater redox potential (not lower), and PS I does not oxidize water. Water oxidation is linked solely to PS II.
- The claim regarding the reduction of pyridine nucleotide is accurate; the downhill flow of electrons from the terminal acceptor reduces \(\text{NADP}^{+}\) into \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\) via \(\text{NADP}\) reductase.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding downhill flow between photosystems and the reduction of \(\text{NADP}^{+}\) are correct, while the statement linking PS I to water oxidation is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Mechanism and localization of water photolysis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the splitting of water in photosynthesis:

Statement I: The water-splitting complex is physically associated with Photosystem II and is located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.

Statement II: The protons and molecular oxygen produced by water oxidation are released directly into the stroma of the chloroplast.

Statement III: The electrons generated from water photolysis supply the replacements for electrons lost by the reaction centre of Photosystem II.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photolysis of water provides a continuous source of replacement electrons to oxidized \(\text{P}_{680}\), concurrently generating protons and molecular oxygen at the luminal surface of the thylakoid membrane.

Step 2: Evaluation of Water Splitting Characteristics
- The claim regarding the association and topology of the oxygen-evolving complex is accurate; it is physically bound to PS II on the luminal (inner) face of the thylakoid membrane.
- The claim asserting that protons and oxygen are released into the stroma is inaccurate; because the water-splitting site is on the inner side of the membrane, protons and oxygen are released into the thylakoid lumen.
- The claim regarding electron replenishment is accurate; electrons extracted from water continuously reduce the photo-oxidized \(\text{P}_{680}\) reaction center of PS II.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements specifying the inner membrane localization of PS II-associated splitting and the role of electrons in replenishing PS II are correct, while the statement claiming release into the stroma is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q07 - Characteristics of cyclic photophosphorylation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding cyclic photophosphorylation:

Statement I: Cyclic electron flow operates predominantly in the stroma lamellae membranes, which lack PS II and NADP reductase enzyme.

Statement II: Cyclic photophosphorylation generates both ATP and \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\) without splitting water.

Statement III: Cyclic photophosphorylation is favored when only light of wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) is available for excitation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cyclic photophosphorylation involves electron circulation strictly around PS I, occurring in membranes deficient in PS II and \(\text{NADP}\) reductase, driving ATP formation via proton translocations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cyclic Flow Features
- The claim regarding stroma lamellae characteristics is accurate; stroma thylakoids lack PS II and \(\text{NADP}\) reductase, preventing non-cyclic electron transport.
- The claim stating that both ATP and NADPH are synthesized is inaccurate; cyclic electron flow produces only ATP, with neither \(\text{NADPH}\) formation nor photolysis of water occurring.
- The claim regarding excitation wavelength is accurate; wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) preferentially excite \(\text{P}_{700}\) of PS I, thereby inducing cyclic photophosphorylation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding stroma lamellae enzyme deficiencies and long-wavelength activation are correct, while the statement claiming synthesis of NADPH is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q08 - Development of proton gradient in chemiosmosis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the development of the proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane during chemiosmosis:

Statement I: Protons generated by the photolysis of water accumulate in the thylakoid lumen.

Statement II: The primary electron acceptor of PS II transfers its electron to an H carrier, which abstracts a proton from the stroma and releases it into the lumen.

Statement III: The reduction of \(\text{NADP}^{+}\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\) on the lumen side increases the proton concentration inside the lumen.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The thylakoid proton gradient is established through three coordinated events: vectorially directed water splitting, proton pumping via mobile quinone carriers, and enzymatic proton consumption on the stromal face.

Step 2: Evaluation of Proton Flux Mechanisms
- The claim regarding water photolysis is accurate; the catalytic center on the luminal face releases protons directly into the thylakoid lumen.
- The claim regarding the hydrogen carrier is accurate; the electron carrier transfers electrons to plastoquinone, which takes up protons from the stroma and delivers them to the lumen upon electron passage.
- The claim regarding \(\text{NADP}\) reductase location is inaccurate; \(\text{NADP}\) reductase is situated on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane, where it removes protons from the stroma, decreasing stromal proton concentration rather than accumulating protons in the lumen.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding proton release by water photolysis and proton translocation by the hydrogen carrier are correct, while the statement locating \(\text{NADP}\) reduction in the lumen is incorrect.

answer.text: Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q09 - Subunit structure and catalytic mechanism of ATP synthase

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the ATP synthase enzyme of chloroplasts:

Statement I: The \(\text{CF}_{0}\) portion is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane channel that carries out facilitated diffusion of protons.

Statement II: The \(\text{CF}_{1}\) portion protrudes on the outer surface of the thylakoid membrane facing the stroma.

Statement III: Protons actively pump from the stroma to the lumen through \(\text{CF}_{0}\) using energy released from ATP hydrolysis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chloroplastic ATP synthase utilizes the dissipation of a transmembrane electrochemical proton gradient to catalyze the phosphorylation of ADP to ATP.

Step 2: Evaluation of ATP Synthase Components
- The claim regarding \(\text{CF}_{0}\) is accurate; \(\text{CF}_{0}\) is an integral membrane protein complex forming a transmembrane hydrophilic pore that enables facilitated diffusion of protons down their concentration gradient.
- The claim regarding \(\text{CF}_{1}\) orientation is accurate; \(\text{CF}_{1}\) is a peripheral catalytic complex that protrudes on the stromal face of the thylakoid membrane.
- The claim describing proton pumping through \(\text{CF}_{0}\) is inaccurate; protons move passively through \(\text{CF}_{0}\) from the lumen to the stroma along their gradient. This passive dissipation drives a conformational change in \(\text{CF}_{1}\) for ATP synthesis, rather than consuming ATP to pump protons.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding the transmembrane channel role of \(\text{CF}_{0}\) and the stromal orientation of \(\text{CF}_{1}\) are correct, while the statement describing ATP-driven active pumping is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q10 - Primary acceptor and carboxylation in Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the carboxylation phase of the Calvin cycle:

Statement I: The primary acceptor of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) is a \(5\)-carbon ketose sugar, ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP).

Statement II: The carboxylation of RuBP yields two molecules of \(3\)-phosphoglyceric acid (\(3\)-PGA) and is catalysed by RuBisCO.

Statement III: The Calvin cycle occurs exclusively in \(C_{3}\) plants and is completely replaced by a non-cyclic pathway in \(C_{4}\) plants.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Carboxylation is the fundamental rate-limiting step of the photosynthetic carbon reduction cycle, utilizing RuBisCO to fix atmospheric carbon dioxide into a 3-carbon phosphorylated organic acid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Carboxylation Characteristics
- The claim regarding the \(\text{CO}_{2}\) acceptor molecule is accurate; RuBP is a 5-carbon phosphorylated ketose sugar.
- The claim regarding the product and enzyme is accurate; carboxylation of one RuBP molecule produces two molecules of 3-PGA via RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO).
- The claim regarding species restriction is inaccurate; the Calvin cycle operates as the universal biosynthetic pathway of carbohydrate synthesis in all photosynthetic plants, occurring in mesophyll cells of \(C_{3}\) plants and in bundle sheath cells of \(C_{4}\) plants.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding the identity of RuBP and the enzyme-mediated formation of 3-PGA are correct, while the statement restricting the cycle exclusively to \(C_{3}\) plants is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q11 - Stoichiometry and energetics of the Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the energetic balance sheet of the Calvin cycle:

Statement I: For every molecule of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) fixed, the reduction stage requires \(2\) molecules of ATP and \(2\) molecules of NADPH.

Statement II: Regeneration of the \(\text{CO}_{2}\) acceptor molecule RuBP requires \(1\) molecule of ATP per \(\text{CO}_{2}\) fixed.

Statement III: Synthesis of one molecule of glucose requires \(6\) turns of the cycle, consuming a net total of \(12\text{ ATP}\) and \(18\text{ NADPH}\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The net chemical equation of the Calvin cycle links photochemical energy consumption (ATP and NADPH) to the fixation of inorganic carbon into hexose sugar.

Step 2: Quantitative Evaluation of Cycle Energetics
- The claim regarding the reduction step stoichiometry is accurate; reducing two molecules of 3-PGA to triose phosphate requires 2 ATP for phosphorylation and 2 NADPH for reduction per fixed \(\text{CO}_{2}\).
- The claim regarding regeneration phosphorylation is accurate; converting triose phosphate intermediates back to RuBP utilizes 1 ATP per turn.
- The claim regarding the net balance sheet for one hexose molecule is inaccurate; six turns of the cycle consume \(6 \times 3 = 18\text{ ATP}\) and \(6 \times 2 = 12\text{ NADPH}\), not 12 ATP and 18 NADPH (the values for ATP and NADPH are inverted).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding the per-\(\text{CO}_{2}\) energetic requirements of reduction and regeneration are correct, while the statement detailing the hexose balance sheet is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q12 - Anatomical and enzymatic specialization in C4 plants

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the structural and biochemical features of \(C_{4}\) plants:

Statement I: Bundle sheath cells possess thick walls that are impervious to gaseous exchange and lack intercellular spaces.

Statement II: Mesophyll cells of \(C_{4}\) plants possess high activity of PEP carboxylase but lack the RuBisCO enzyme.

Statement III: Bundle sheath cells are rich in PEP carboxylase but lack RuBisCO, enabling them to fix atmospheric \(\text{CO}_{2}\) directly.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
\(C_{4}\) plants employ Kranz anatomy to segregate the initial carboxylation and the final reductive Calvin cycle between two distinct, specialized tissue compartments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cell Specializations
- The claim regarding bundle sheath structural anatomy is accurate; bundle sheath cells have thick walls lacking intercellular spaces and are impervious to gases, which prevents back-diffusion of concentrated \(\text{CO}_{2}\).
- The claim regarding mesophyll enzyme distribution is accurate; mesophyll cells contain PEPcase to fix bicarbonate into oxaloacetic acid, but completely lack RuBisCO.
- The claim regarding bundle sheath enzyme complement is inaccurate; bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO and completely lack PEPcase, fixing \(\text{CO}_{2}\) released from decarboxylation of imported \(C_{4}\) acids.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements describing bundle sheath anatomical properties and mesophyll enzyme content are correct, while the statement asserting bundle sheath cells contain PEPcase is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q13 - Molecular mechanism of photorespiration in C3 plants

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the phenomenon of photorespiration:

Statement I: When oxygen binds to RuBisCO in \(C_{3}\) plants, RuBP is converted into one molecule of \(3\)-phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate.

Statement II: The photorespiratory pathway produces neither sugars nor ATP/NADPH, but instead releases \(\text{CO}_{2}\) with the consumption of ATP.

Statement III: In \(C_{4}\) plants, photorespiration is suppressed because the decarboxylation of \(C_{4}\) acids in bundle sheath cells elevates \(\text{CO}_{2}\) concentration around RuBisCO.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photorespiration (\(C_{2}\) cycle) is a competitive oxygenase reaction driven by RuBisCO under low \(\text{CO}_{2}\) to \(\text{O}_{2}\) ratios, causing carbon loss in \(C_{3}\) plants that is overcome by the carbon-concentrating mechanism of \(C_{4}\) plants.

Step 2: Evaluation of Photorespiratory Mechanisms
- The claim regarding the enzymatic cleavage of RuBP during oxygenation is accurate; oxygenation of RuBP by RuBisCO yields one molecule of 3-PGA (3 carbons) and one molecule of 2-phosphoglycolate (2 carbons).
- The claim regarding energy yield is accurate; photorespiration does not synthesize ATP or NADPH, nor does it produce carbohydrates, but wastes chemical energy by releasing previously fixed carbon as \(\text{CO}_{2}\) with consumption of ATP.
- The claim explaining photorespiratory suppression in \(C_{4}\) plants is accurate; transport and decarboxylation of malic/aspartic acid within bundle sheath cells maintains a high local \(\text{CO}_{2}\) concentration, thereby outcompeting \(\text{O}_{2}\) for the active site of RuBisCO.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All three statements accurately characterize the biochemical reactions and biological significance of photorespiration. Therefore, all three statements are correct.

answer.text: I, II, and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q14 - External and limiting factors affecting photosynthetic rates

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding factors affecting photosynthesis:

Statement I: According to Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, if a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, its rate is determined by the factor nearest to its minimal value.

Statement II: Light saturation occurs at approximately \(10\%\) of full sunlight, meaning light is rarely a limiting factor for plants in open natural habitats.

Statement III: \(C_{4}\) plants achieve \(\text{CO}_{2}\) saturation only beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\), whereas \(C_{3}\) plants saturate at around \(360\ \mu\text{L}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photosynthesis is regulated by concurrent environmental parameters (light, \(\text{CO}_{2}\), temperature, water) governed by Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, with distinct response thresholds in \(C_{3}\) and \(C_{4}\) plants.

Step 2: Evaluation of Factor Limits
- The formulation of Blackman's Law is accurate; the rate of a multi-factorial biological process is limited by whichever variable is present at the sub-optimal level closest to its minimum.
- The statement regarding light saturation is accurate; photosynthetic light saturation typically occurs at roughly 10 percent of full sunlight, making light non-limiting except in dense understories or heavy shade.
- The claim comparing \(\text{CO}_{2}\) saturation levels is inaccurate; \(C_{4}\) plants saturate at lower \(\text{CO}_{2}\) concentrations (around \(360\ \mu\text{L}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\)), while \(C_{3}\) plants saturate only at elevated levels beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\). The stated saturation thresholds are reversed.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the statements regarding Blackman's Law and light saturation values are correct, while the statement giving inverted carbon dioxide saturation values is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I and III are correct
Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
I, II, and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q01 - Milestones in early photosynthesis experiments

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding early experiments that established the fundamental concepts of photosynthesis:

  1. Joseph Priestley hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove, and he discovered oxygen in 1774.
  2. Jan Ingenhousz showed that in bright sunlight, small bubbles of oxygen were formed around the non-green parts of an aquatic plant.
  3. Julius von Sachs provided evidence that the green parts of plants produce glucose, which is usually stored as starch.
  4. T.W. Engelmann used a prism to split light and observed that aerobic bacteria clustered around the green alga Cladophora mainly in the green and yellow regions of the spectrum.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Priestley's experiments
Joseph Priestley observed that a burning candle or a breathing animal in a bell jar fouled the air, extinguishing the flame and suffocating the mouse. Placing a mint plant in the bell jar kept the mouse alive and allowed the candle to burn, leading to the hypothesis that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove. Priestley discovered oxygen in 1774. Thus, this historical proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ingenhousz's findings
Jan Ingenhousz demonstrated that sunlight is indispensable for air purification. Using an aquatic plant in bright sunlight, he observed that oxygen bubbles formed exclusively around the green parts of the plant, whereas no bubbles formed in the dark. Because oxygen release is confined to green parts rather than non-green parts, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Sachs's contribution
In 1854, Julius von Sachs established that the growing parts of plants produce glucose, which is stored in the form of starch. He also showed that chlorophyll is situated within specialized bodies (later identified as chloroplasts) inside green plant cells. Thus, this proposition is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of Engelmann's action spectrum
T.W. Engelmann illuminated the green alga Cladophora with light split into its spectral components using a prism. Using aerobic bacteria to identify sites of oxygen evolution, he observed that the bacteria congregated primarily in the blue and red illumination zones, not the green and yellow zones, delineating the first action spectrum of photosynthesis. Thus, this proposition is inaccurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the statements describing Priestley's hypothesis and Sachs's demonstration of starch formation are conceptually valid, whereas those concerning Ingenhousz's bubble formation on non-green tissue and Engelmann's bacterial congregation in green-yellow light are incorrect.

answer.text: I and III only
I and II only
II and IV only
I, III, and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q02 - Chloroplast pigments and light harvesting complexes

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding photosynthetic pigments and the light harvesting complex (LHC):

  1. Paper chromatography reveals that leaf colour is due to four pigments: chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids.
  2. Chlorophyll a constitutes the reaction centre, absorbing maximally in the green region of the visible light spectrum.
  3. Accessory pigments absorb wider ranges of wavelengths and protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
  4. The reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm in Photosystem II and 680 nm in Photosystem I.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of chromatographic separation of pigments
Chromatographic analysis of leaf extract demonstrates four major pigment classes: chlorophyll a (blue-green), chlorophyll b (yellow-green), xanthophylls (yellow), and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Hence, this proposition is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of chlorophyll a absorption peaks
Chlorophyll a shows sharp absorption peaks in the blue and red regions of the visible spectrum, showing minimum absorption in the green region, which is reflected. Thus, the claim that it absorbs maximally in the green region is factually incorrect.

Step 3: Role of accessory pigments
Chlorophyll b, carotenoids, and xanthophylls function as accessory pigments. They harvest photon energy across spectral wavelengths not efficiently captured by chlorophyll a, transfer the excitation energy to chlorophyll a, and shield chlorophyll a against destructive photo-oxidation. Hence, this proposition is accurate.

Step 4: Identification of photosystem reaction centres
In Photosystem I (PS I), the reaction centre chlorophyll a molecule has an absorption maximum at 700 nm (\(\text{P}_{700}\)), whereas in Photosystem II (PS II), the absorption maximum is at 680 nm (\(\text{P}_{680}\)). The proposition inverts these designations and is therefore incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Only the statements addressing pigment chromatographic separation and the protective, light-harvesting function of accessory pigments are correct.

answer.text: I and II only
I and III only
II and IV only
III and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q03 - Cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation characteristics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements concerning cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation in chloroplasts:

  1. In non-cyclic photophosphorylation, both Photosystem I and Photosystem II operate in series connected via an electron transport chain.
  2. The water-splitting complex is physically located on the stroma-facing outer surface of the thylakoid membrane.
  3. Stroma lamellae membranes lack Photosystem II as well as the NADP reductase enzyme.
  4. Cyclic photophosphorylation results in the net synthesis of both ATP and \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of non-cyclic electron transport scheme
In non-cyclic photophosphorylation (the Z-scheme), electrons flow from water through PS II, pass along an electron transport chain consisting of cytochromes to PS I, and are ultimately transferred to \(\text{NADP}^{+}\). Both photosystems operate in series. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of water-splitting complex location
The oxygen-evolving water-splitting complex is associated with PS II and is situated on the inner side (lumen side) of the thylakoid membrane, releasing protons and oxygen into the thylakoid lumen rather than the stroma. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of stroma lamellae composition
While the appressed granal lamellae possess both PS I and PS II, the non-appressed stroma lamellae lack PS II and lack NADP reductase enzyme. Consequently, excited electrons cycle back to PS I through the electron transport chain. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of cyclic photophosphorylation products
Because the stroma lamellae lack NADP reductase and PS II, cyclic electron flow circulates electrons within PS I only. As a result, cyclic photophosphorylation yields exclusively ATP and does not synthesize \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\). Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are those identifying the series connection of photosystems in non-cyclic flow and the absence of PS II and NADP reductase in stroma lamellae membranes.

answer.text: I and II only
I and III only
II and IV only
I, III, and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q04 - Chemiosmotic mechanism of ATP generation

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding the chemiosmotic hypothesis of ATP synthesis in chloroplasts:

  1. Photolysis of water occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, contributing to proton accumulation in the lumen.
  2. The primary electron acceptor from PS II transfers its electron to an H carrier, removing a proton from the stroma and releasing it into the lumen.
  3. The enzyme NADP reductase is located on the lumen side of the thylakoid membrane, increasing lumen proton concentration.
  4. Protons move down their electrochemical gradient from the lumen to the stroma through the transmembrane channel of \(\text{CF}_{0}\) of ATP synthase.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of photolysis and lumen proton accumulation
Water-splitting is localized to the inner side of the thylakoid membrane. Consequently, the resulting protons (\(\text{H}^{+}\)) accumulate directly within the thylakoid lumen, elevating the proton concentration and decreasing the lumen pH. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of electron carrier coupled proton translocation
The primary electron acceptor from PS II is located on the outer side of the membrane and transfers its electron to an \(\text{H}\) carrier (plastoquinone). Plastoquinone picks up a proton from the stroma when accepting the electron. As it transfers its electron to the cytochrome complex on the inner surface, the proton is discharged into the lumen. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of NADP reductase location
The enzyme NADP reductase is physically positioned on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane. It abstracts protons from the stroma along with electrons from PS I to reduce \(\text{NADP}^{+}\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^{+}\), thereby reducing stroma proton concentration rather than increasing lumen protons. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of ATP synthase function and proton translocation
Protons accumulated in the lumen flow down their concentration gradient into the stroma via facilitated diffusion through the \(\text{CF}_{0}\) transmembrane channel of ATP synthase. This dissipation of the proton gradient triggers conformational changes in the \(\text{CF}_{1}\) catalytic headpiece facing the stroma, driving ATP synthesis. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Propositions describing water splitting in the lumen, proton pumping by the plastoquinone shuttle, and proton movement via \(\text{CF}_0\) to the stroma are correct, whereas the proposition placing NADP reductase on the lumen side is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, and III only
I, II, and IV only
II, III, and IV only
I and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q05 - Calvin cycle stages and energetic stoichiometry

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the Calvin cycle (\(\text{C}_{3}\) pathway):

  1. Carboxylation of RuBP yields two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA) and is catalysed by RuBisCO.
  2. The primary \(\text{CO}_{2}\) acceptor molecule in the Calvin cycle is a 2-carbon compound called ribulose bisphosphate.
  3. Reduction of each molecule of fixed \(\text{CO}_{2}\) requires 2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH.
  4. Regeneration of the \(\text{CO}_{2}\) acceptor RuBP requires 2 molecules of ATP per RuBP regenerated.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of carboxylation step
Carboxylation is the addition of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) to the acceptor ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP), catalysed by RuBisCO. This reaction yields two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA), a 3-carbon stable organic acid. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the primary carbon dioxide acceptor structure
The primary carbon dioxide acceptor, RuBP, is a 5-carbon ketose sugar, not a 2-carbon compound. Melvin Calvin and co-workers initially sought a 2-carbon compound but proved that RuBP has five carbons. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the energetic requirements of reduction
The reduction stage entails a series of enzymatic steps converting 3-PGA to triose phosphate. This utilizes 2 molecules of ATP (for phosphorylation) and 2 molecules of NADPH (for reduction) for each molecule of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) fixed. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of RuBP regeneration energetics
The regeneration stage requires phosphorylation of intermediate sugars to regenerate RuBP so that the cycle continues uninterrupted. This step consumes 1 molecule of ATP for each RuBP regenerated, not 2 molecules of ATP. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statements detailing the carboxylation of RuBP to form two 3-PGA molecules and the consumption of 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per \(\text{CO}_{2}\) during reduction are correct, whereas statements proposing a 2-carbon acceptor and 2 ATP per RuBP regeneration are incorrect.

answer.text: I and III only
I and II only
II and IV only
I, III, and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q06 - Kranz anatomy and the Hatch Slack pathway

questiontext.text:
Examine the following four statements regarding \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants and the Hatch and Slack pathway:

  1. The bundle sheath cells possess thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, lack intercellular spaces, and contain a large number of chloroplasts.
  2. The primary carboxylation reaction occurs in the mesophyll cells where \(\text{CO}_{2}\) combines with phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) catalysed by PEP carboxylase.
  3. Mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants are rich in RuBisCO but lack PEP carboxylase.
  4. Decarboxylation of the \(\text{C}_{4}\) acid occurs in the bundle sheath cells, releasing \(\text{CO}_{2}\) that enters the Calvin cycle.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of bundle sheath cell anatomy
Kranz anatomy is defined by concentric rings of large bundle sheath cells surrounding the vascular bundles. These cells have thick walls impervious to gas diffusion, devoid of intercellular gaps, and packed with abundant chloroplasts. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of primary carboxylation in mesophyll
In \(\text{C}_{4}\) leaves, the initial carbon dioxide fixation takes place in the mesophyll cytoplasm. Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP, a 3-carbon compound) fixes bicarbonate to generate oxaloacetic acid (OAA, a 4-carbon acid) under catalysis by PEP carboxylase (PEPcase). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of enzyme distribution between cell types
Mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants contain PEP carboxylase but completely lack RuBisCO. In contrast, bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO but lack PEPcase. The statement reverses this relationship and is therefore inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of decarboxylation in bundle sheath cells
Malic acid or aspartic acid (\(\text{C}_{4}\) acids) is transported from the mesophyll into the bundle sheath cells via plasmodesmata. There, decarboxylation releases \(\text{CO}_{2}\) and a 3-carbon acid. The released \(\text{CO}_{2}\) is immediately fixed by RuBisCO in the Calvin cycle operating in the bundle sheath cells. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Propositions detailing the anatomical features of bundle sheath cells, initial carboxylation via PEPcase in mesophyll cells, and bundle sheath decarboxylation are correct, whereas the proposition claiming mesophyll cells are rich in RuBisCO is incorrect.

answer.text: I and II only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q07 - Mechanism and biological impact of photorespiration

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding photorespiration and enzyme kinetics of RuBisCO:

  1. RuBisCO exhibits a much greater affinity for \(\text{CO}_{2}\) than for \(\text{O}_{2}\) when the concentrations of both gases are nearly equal.
  2. In the oxygenase reaction of RuBisCO, RuBP binds with \(\text{O}_{2}\) to produce two molecules of phosphoglycolate.
  3. The photorespiratory pathway does not synthesize sugars, ATP, or NADPH, but instead consumes ATP and releases \(\text{CO}_{2}\).
  4. \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants undergo high rates of photorespiration at elevated temperatures due to high oxygen accumulation in bundle sheath cells.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of RuBisCO substrate affinity
RuBisCO possesses competitive active sites capable of interacting with both \(\text{CO}_{2}\) and \(\text{O}_{2}\). When the ratio of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) to \(\text{O}_{2}\) is nearly equal, RuBisCO exhibits a significantly higher binding affinity for \(\text{CO}_{2}\) than for \(\text{O}_{2}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of products in the oxygenation of RuBP
When oxygen binds to the active site of RuBisCO, RuBP (a 5-carbon compound) is cleaved into one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate (3 carbons) and one molecule of 2-phosphoglycolate (2 carbons), not two molecules of phosphoglycolate. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of energy yield in photorespiration
The photorespiratory pathway is an energetically wasteful process: it fails to generate ATP or NADPH, does not yield sugars, and causes the loss of previously fixed carbon as \(\text{CO}_{2}\) while consuming ATP. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of photorespiration in C4 plants
In \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants, photorespiration is virtually absent because decarboxylation of \(\text{C}_{4}\) acid inside bundle sheath cells elevates the local concentration of \(\text{CO}_{2}\) around RuBisCO. This high \(\text{CO}_{2}\) environment competitively suppresses the oxygenase activity of RuBisCO. Thus, the assertion that \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants display high photorespiration is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statements highlighting RuBisCO's greater affinity for \(\text{CO}_{2}\) under equal concentrations and the non-productive, ATP-consuming nature of the photorespiratory cycle are correct.

answer.text: I and III only
I and II only
II and IV only
I, III, and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER11_MCQ_Q08 - External factors governing photosynthetic rate

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding factors affecting photosynthesis:

  1. According to Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, if a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, its rate is determined by the factor nearest to its minimal value.
  2. Light saturation occurs at approximately 10 per cent of full sunlight; therefore, light is rarely a limiting factor for plants in nature, except for shade-dwelling plants or those in dense canopies.
  3. \(\text{C}_{4}\) plants show \(\text{CO}_{2}\) saturation at about \(360\,\mu\text{L}\,\text{L}^{-1}\), whereas \(\text{C}_{3}\) plants saturate only beyond \(450\,\mu\text{L}\,\text{L}^{-1}\).
  4. Water stress directly inhibits the photochemical light reactions by limiting the substrate water required for photolysis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Blackman's law
Blackman (1905) formulated the Law of Limiting Factors: when multiple factors govern a biochemical process, the rate is constrained by the factor available at sub-optimal levels (nearest to its minimum value), which directly alters the rate if its availability changes. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of light saturation threshold
Light saturation for photosynthetic carbon assimilation occurs at roughly 10% of full sunlight. Because available ambient light usually exceeds this intensity, light is seldom the factor limiting photosynthesis in nature, except in dense forests or under deep shade. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of carbon dioxide saturation in C3 and C4 plants
\(\text{C}_{4}\) plants saturate at lower \(\text{CO}_{2}\) levels of approximately \(360\,\mu\text{L}\,\text{L}^{-1}\) due to the efficiency of the PEPcase pumping mechanism, whereas \(\text{C}_{3}\) plants show saturation only above \(450\,\mu\text{L}\,\text{L}^{-1}\). Current atmospheric levels (\(300\text{--}400\,\mu\text{L}\,\text{L}^{-1}\)) are limiting to \(\text{C}_{3}\) plants. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the physiological impact of water stress
Although water is a chemical reactant in photolysis, water stress primarily affects photosynthesis indirectly: it causes stomata to close (reducing \(\text{CO}_{2}\) entry) and induces leaf wilting (reducing surface area and slowing metabolic activity), rather than by direct substrate limitation in photolysis. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The statements regarding Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, light saturation at 10% of full sunlight, and comparative \(\text{CO}_{2}\) saturation values between \(\text{C}_{4}\) and \(\text{C}_{3}\) plants are correct, whereas the statement attributing the effect of water stress to substrate exhaustion in light reactions is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, and III only
I and II only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Milestones in early experiments on photosynthesis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding early experiments in photosynthesis:

(I) Joseph Priestley hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove.
(II) Jan Ingenhousz showed that in the dark, small bubbles were formed around the green parts of an aquatic plant, while in bright sunlight they did not.
(III) Julius von Sachs provided evidence that glucose is produced when plants grow and is usually stored as starch.
(IV) T.W. Engelmann used a prism to split light and observed that aerobic bacteria accumulated mainly in the green and yellow regions of the split spectrum.
(V) Cornelius van Niel inferred that the \(\text{O}_2\) evolved by green plants comes from \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), not from carbon dioxide.

How many of the given statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding Priestley's hypothesis
Joseph Priestley observed that a burning candle or a breathing mouse fouled the air in a closed bell jar, whereas introducing a mint plant allowed the mouse to survive and the candle to burn. From this, he hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding Ingenhousz's aquatic plant experiment
Jan Ingenhousz demonstrated that in bright sunlight, small bubbles were formed around the green parts of an aquatic plant, whereas in the dark, these bubbles did not form. These bubbles were later identified as oxygen. The claim that bubbles formed in the dark rather than in sunlight reverses the experimental findings, making this statement inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding Julius von Sachs's findings
Julius von Sachs showed in 1854 that the green substance in plants is located in special bodies (later termed chloroplasts) where glucose is made, and that this glucose is usually stored in the form of starch. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding Engelmann's experiment
T.W. Engelmann split light using a prism and illuminated the green alga Cladophora in a suspension of aerobic bacteria. He observed that the bacteria congregated primarily in the regions of blue and red light of the spectrum where oxygen evolution was greatest, not in the green and yellow regions. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding Cornelius van Niel's formulation
Based on his studies of purple and green sulfur bacteria, Cornelius van Niel demonstrated that photosynthesis is a light-dependent reaction where hydrogen from an oxidisable substrate reduces carbon dioxide. Because sulfur or sulfate is produced when \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\) is used instead of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), he concluded that the oxygen released by green plants originates from water and not from carbon dioxide. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
Counting the valid evaluations confirms that the findings related to Priestley, Sachs, and van Niel are scientifically correct, while those related to Ingenhousz and Engelmann are incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly three statements are correct.

Only three

All five

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Organization and absorption spectra of photosynthetic pigments

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements concerning photosynthetic pigments and light harvesting complexes:

(I) A chromatographic separation of leaf pigments reveals that chlorophyll a appears bright or blue-green, whereas chlorophyll b appears yellow-green.
(II) Accessory pigments such as chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids enable a wider range of wavelengths of light to be utilised and protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
(III) The light harvesting complex (LHC) within each photosystem is made up of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins, including the single reaction centre chlorophyll a molecule.
(IV) In Photosystem I, the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at \(700\text{ nm}\), whereas in Photosystem II it absorbs maximally at \(680\text{ nm}\).
(V) The action spectrum of photosynthesis shows an absolute, complete one-to-one overlap with the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a across all wavelengths.

Which of the following combinations contains all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding chromatographic separation of leaf pigments
Paper chromatography demonstrates that leaf colour is due to four pigments: chlorophyll a (bright or blue-green), chlorophyll b (yellow-green), xanthophylls (yellow), and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the role of accessory pigments
Accessory pigments (chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids) absorb light at wavelengths other than those absorbed by chlorophyll a and transfer that energy to the reaction centre. They also shield chlorophyll a from damage caused by photo-oxidation. Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding light harvesting complex organisation
Each photosystem possesses hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins that form the antenna or light harvesting complex; however, this complex excludes the single chlorophyll a molecule that specifically constitutes the reaction centre. Therefore, asserting that the antenna includes the reaction centre molecule is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding reaction centre absorption peaks
In Photosystem I (PS I), the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption maximum at \(700\text{ nm}\) (designated \(\text{P}_{700}\)), whereas in Photosystem II (PS II), it absorbs maximally at \(680\text{ nm}\) (designated \(\text{P}_{680}\)). Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding spectrum overlap
Although the action spectrum of photosynthesis shows prominent peaks in the blue and red regions matching chlorophyll a, there is not a complete one-to-one overlap because accessory pigments also absorb light at intermediate wavelengths. Hence, claiming an absolute one-to-one overlap is inaccurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The evaluations confirm that the statements concerning leaf pigment colors, accessory pigment functions, and photosystem absorption peaks are correct.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (II), and (IV) only represents the valid set.

answer.text: (I), (II), and (IV) only
(II), (III), and (V) only
(I), (III), and (IV) only
(I), (II), and (V) only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation characteristics

questiontext.text:
Examine the following five statements regarding cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation:

(I) In non-cyclic electron transport, electrons excited from PS II pass downhill along a redox potential scale through an electron transport system of cytochromes to PS I.
(II) The water-splitting complex is physically associated with PS II and is located on the outer surface of the thylakoid membrane facing the stroma.
(III) Stroma lamellae membranes possess PS I but lack PS II as well as the \(\text{NADP}\) reductase enzyme.
(IV) Cyclic photophosphorylation results in the synthesis of both \(\text{ATP}\) and \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\).
(V) Cyclic electron flow occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) is available for excitation.

How many of the given statements are INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding electron transport from PS II to PS I
In non-cyclic photophosphorylation, light absorption at \(680\text{ nm}\) excites electrons in PS II, which are accepted by an electron acceptor and passed downhill through an electron transport chain containing cytochromes to PS I. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the location of the water-splitting complex
The water-splitting complex is associated with PS II, which is physically located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane facing the lumen. Because protons and oxygen are released into the lumen and not onto the stroma-facing outer surface, placing it on the outer side is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding stroma lamellae composition
While granal thylakoid membranes contain both PS I and PS II, the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II and \(\text{NADP}\) reductase, retaining only PS I. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding cyclic photophosphorylation products
In cyclic photophosphorylation, excited electrons cycle back to the PS I reaction centre through the electron transport chain without moving to \(\text{NADP}^+\). Consequently, cyclic photophosphorylation produces only \(\text{ATP}\) and does not generate \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\). Thus, claiming both are produced is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding wavelength requirements for cyclic flow
When wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) illuminate the chloroplast, PS II is not effectively excited, leaving only PS I operational. Under these conditions, cyclic electron flow and photophosphorylation take place. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
Among the five statements, two statements—the one describing the location of the water-splitting complex and the one asserting that cyclic photophosphorylation synthesises \(\text{NADPH}\)—are incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly two statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Only one

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Mechanism of chemiosmotic ATP synthesis in chloroplasts

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the chemiosmotic hypothesis in chloroplasts:

(I) Protons produced by the photolysis of water accumulate in the thylakoid lumen, resulting in a measurable decrease in lumen \(\text{pH}\).
(II) The primary electron acceptor from PS II transfers its electron to a hydrogen carrier, which removes a proton from the stroma and releases it into the lumen.
(III) The enzyme \(\text{NADP}\) reductase is located on the lumen side of the thylakoid membrane and releases protons into the lumen.
(IV) The \(\text{CF}_0\) component of \(\text{ATP}\) synthase is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane channel for facilitated diffusion of protons.
(V) Movement of protons through \(\text{CF}_0\) occurs from the stroma into the lumen, activating the catalytic \(\text{CF}_1\) particle on the lumen side.

Which of the following combinations includes all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding photolysis and lumen proton accumulation
Water photolysis occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, directly dumping protons into the thylakoid lumen. This proton build-up increases proton concentration and lowers lumen \(\text{pH}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the hydrogen carrier
The primary electron acceptor of PS II is located towards the outer side of the membrane and passes its electron to an \(\text{H}\) carrier (plastoquinone). This molecule picks up a proton from the stroma; when it transfers its electron to an inner electron carrier, it discharges the proton into the lumen. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding NADP reductase orientation
The \(\text{NADP}\) reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane. It extracts protons from the stroma along with electrons from PS I to reduce \(\text{NADP}^+\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\), thereby depleting stroma protons rather than releasing them into the lumen. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding the structure and role of CF0
\(\text{ATP}\) synthase consists of \(\text{CF}_0\), an integral transmembrane channel embedded within the thylakoid membrane that facilitates proton diffusion across the membrane, and \(\text{CF}_1\), which protrudes into the stroma. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding proton direction during ATP generation
Protons flow down the electrochemical gradient from the lumen back into the stroma through the \(\text{CF}_0\) channel. This flow drives a conformational shift in the \(\text{CF}_1\) unit facing the stroma to produce \(\text{ATP}\). Stating that protons move from stroma to lumen reverses the established direction. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements detailing water photolysis, hydrogen-carrier mediated proton pumping, and \(\text{CF}_0\) transmembrane architecture are correct.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (II), and (IV) only represents the correct set.

answer.text: (I), (III), and (IV) only
(II), (IV), and (V) only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Energetics and stages of the Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Read the following statements regarding the Calvin cycle (\(\text{C}_3\) pathway):

(I) Carboxylation is the most crucial step of the cycle, in which \(\text{CO}_2\) is fixed by ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (\(\text{RuBP}\)) to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (\(\text{3-PGA}\)).
(II) The reduction stage involves the utilisation of \(2\) molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation and \(2\) molecules of \(\text{NADPH}\) for reduction per \(\text{CO}_2\) molecule fixed.
(III) For the net synthesis of one molecule of glucose, \(6\) turns of the cycle are required, consuming a net total of \(12\text{ ATP}\) and \(12\text{ NADPH}\).
(IV) Regeneration of the primary \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor \(\text{RuBP}\) requires the expenditure of two molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) per \(\text{RuBP}\) regenerated.
(V) The Calvin cycle operates in all photosynthetic plants, irrespective of whether they possess \(\text{C}_3\) or \(\text{C}_4\) pathways.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding carboxylation
Carboxylation is the fixation of \(\text{CO}_2\) into a stable intermediate. In this step, \(\text{CO}_2\) combines with the 5-carbon ketose sugar \(\text{RuBP}\), catalysed by \(\text{RuBisCO}\), to produce two molecules of 3-carbon \(\text{3-PGA}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding reduction requirements per CO2 fixed
During the reduction stage, each fixed \(\text{CO}_2\) molecule requires \(2\) molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation and \(2\) molecules of \(\text{NADPH}\) for reduction to form triose phosphates. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding overall energetic inputs for one glucose molecule
To produce one molecule of glucose (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)), \(6\) molecules of \(\text{CO}_2\) must be fixed through \(6\) turns of the cycle. Across the whole cycle, this requires \(18\text{ ATP}\) (\(12\text{ ATP}\) in reduction plus \(6\text{ ATP}\) in regeneration) and \(12\text{ NADPH}\), not \(12\text{ ATP}\). Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding ATP requirement during regeneration
The regeneration of the \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor molecule \(\text{RuBP}\) requires one molecule of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation per turn of the cycle, not two. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding occurrence of the Calvin cycle in all photosynthetic plants
The Calvin pathway is the universal biosynthetic pathway for sugar formation in all photosynthetic plants, taking place in the mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_3\) plants and in the bundle sheath cells of \(\text{C}_4\) plants. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements regarding carboxylation, per-\(\text{CO}_2\) reduction stoichiometry, and universal occurrence are scientifically valid, whereas the overall \(\text{ATP}\) count for glucose synthesis and the regeneration stoichiometry are invalid.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly three statements are correct.

answer.text: Only two
Only three
Only four
All five

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Kranz anatomy decarboxylation and photorespiration

questiontext.text:
Examine the following statements regarding the \(\text{C}_4\) pathway and photorespiration:

(I) Bundle sheath cells in \(\text{C}_4\) leaves are characterised by having thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, no intercellular spaces, and a large number of chloroplasts.
(II) In the mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_4\) plants, primary \(\text{CO}_2\) fixation is catalysed by \(\text{RuBisCO}\), forming oxaloacetic acid.
(III) In bundle sheath cells, \(\text{C}_4\) acids are decarboxylated to release \(\text{CO}_2\), which raises the intracellular concentration of \(\text{CO}_2\) and suppresses the oxygenase activity of \(\text{RuBisCO}\).
(IV) In the photorespiratory pathway of \(\text{C}_3\) plants, \(\text{RuBisCO}\) binds \(\text{O}_2\) to convert \(\text{RuBP}\) into one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate, with neither synthesis of sugars nor of \(\text{ATP}\).
(V) \(\text{C}_4\) plants exhibit saturation of photosynthesis at lower atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) concentrations (about \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\)) than \(\text{C}_3\) plants (which saturate beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\)).

Which of the following combinations contains all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding Kranz bundle sheath anatomy
Kranz anatomy in \(\text{C}_4\) plants is characterised by bundle sheath cells arranged in several layers around vascular bundles. These cells possess thick walls that are impervious to gas exchange, lack intercellular spaces, and contain abundant chloroplasts. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding mesophyll carboxylation enzymes
In \(\text{C}_4\) plants, primary carboxylation occurs in the mesophyll cells where phosphoenolpyruvate (\(\text{PEP}\)) fixes \(\text{HCO}_3^-\) via the enzyme \(\text{PEP}\) carboxylase (\(\text{PEPcase}\)). The mesophyll cells lack \(\text{RuBisCO}\). Thus, attributing primary fixation here to \(\text{RuBisCO}\) is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding bundle sheath decarboxylation
Malic acid or aspartic acid transported from mesophyll cells is broken down in bundle sheath cells through decarboxylation, releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and a 3-carbon acid. This mechanism enriches \(\text{CO}_2\) around \(\text{RuBisCO}\), ensuring it functions almost exclusively as a carboxylase and preventing photorespiration. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding the photorespiratory reaction
When \(\text{RuBisCO}\) binds \(\text{O}_2\) in \(\text{C}_3\) plants, \(\text{RuBP}\) is cleaved into one molecule of 3-carbon phosphoglycerate and one molecule of 2-carbon phosphoglycolate. The pathway releases \(\text{CO}_2\) with consumption of \(\text{ATP}\), yielding neither \(\text{ATP}\) nor sugars. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding CO2 saturation thresholds
Under high light intensities, \(\text{C}_4\) plants attain photosynthetic saturation at approximately \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\) of \(\text{CO}_2\), whereas \(\text{C}_3\) plants saturate only above \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The evaluations confirm that the statements describing Kranz anatomy, bundle sheath decarboxylation, photorespiratory stoichiometry, and \(\text{CO}_2\) saturation levels are scientifically valid, while the statement attributing mesophyll fixation to \(\text{RuBisCO}\) is incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (III), (IV), and (V) only represents the valid set.

answer.text: (I), (II), (III), and (IV) only
(II), (III), and (V) only
(I), (III), (IV), and (V) only
(I), (IV), and (V) only
